title: Sierre-Zinal — history
claims: The official history page records that the race was imagined by Jean-Claude Pont, a doctor of mathematics, professor of history and philosophy of science and certified Swiss mountain guide.
The same page states that the race would be named, not just Sierre-Zinal, but the 'Race of the Five 4000 m Peaks'.
The same page names the 'Imperial Crown' as the Weisshorn (4,404 m), Zinalrothorn (4,221 m), Obergabelhorn (4,063 m), Matterhorn (4,478 m) and Dent Blanche (4,357 m).

The same page describes the Tourist category as unique to Sierre-Zinal: it was designed for runners whose sole aim is to get together and test themselves, and it receives a certificate with the final time but no ranking.
The same page summarises that philosophy as 'the heart before the watch'.
The same page refers to Pont's book 'Courir dans une Cathédrale', devoted to the first forty years of the race.

verification.note: 2026-11-08 直取官网英文历史页全文。页面把 Weisshorn 写作 4,404 m；本页只采用五个山峰名称与官方叙述，不把这座山的高度当作已核数值使用。
